data.text: Now I understand the OpenSpec merge algorithm. Let me set up a todo list and start implementing.
Now let me create the fixture cases with a generator script.

Task complete. Both gates pass:

- Task verify: `111 pass / 0 fail`
- Proposal verify (`pnpm verify`): exit 0

Summary of the work:

**`src/core/spec/delta.ts`** — ported OpenSpec 1.13.1's merge so osq now writes exactly what `openspec archive` writes:
- requirement blocks carried verbatim (GIVEN/AND and any other line survive)
- OpenSpec-shaped section parsing/reconstruction, single-blank collapse outside fences
- new capabilities put purpose on the line after `## Purpose`; bases keep untouched bytes
- `### Requirement:` rename form; `DeltaMergeError` for dropped scenarios, existing ADDED names, bare renames (message names the expected form), and unmatched targets

**`tests/openspec-differential.test.ts` + `tests/fixtures/openspec-diff/**`** — ten cases covering ADDED, MODIFIED, REMOVED, RENAMED, new capability, second change, GIVEN/AND, dropped scenario, duplicate ADDED, and bare RENAME; scaffolds two temp repos with the osq schema, runs real `openspec archive` vs `applyOpenSpecDeltas`, and names `openspec 1.13.1` in every assertion.

**Test updates** — header-form RENAMED, new golden, three new refusal tests in `delta-merge.test.ts`; blank-line strip after `## Purpose` in `living-specs-delta-equivalence.test.ts`.

Two deviations are recorded in the result: fixtures use the required local `verify.cjs` instead of the sentinel (the linter's checked-in fixture rule forbids it), and two synthetic 017-replay tests were adapted slightly to stay OpenSpec-compatible while preserving every assertion.
